text: Is your customer and lead data in one connected system, or scattered across different places?

options.label: Scattered: spreadsheets, inboxes, and tools that don't talk to each other
Partially in a CRM but with major gaps and a lot of manual entry
Mostly in one system with some workarounds
One connected system: clean data, automated intake, reliable records

text: How would you describe your website and digital front door?

options.label: Outdated or missing: doesn't reflect what we actually do
Basic presence, but no real way to capture or convert leads
Functional: drives some leads, mostly manual follow-up after that
Optimized: structured intake, tracking in place, automated response

text: How consistent and usable is the data you collect from customers, jobs, or transactions?

options.label: Inconsistent: different formats, missing fields, hard to act on
Mostly collected but not standardized or easy to search
Reasonably clean in our main system, some gaps remain
Structured, complete, and reliable enough to build real systems on top of

text: Is your team using AI to draft, summarize, or generate content as part of actual daily work?

options.label: No: nobody uses AI tools in any structured way
A few people experiment on their own, no shared approach or regular use
Several people use AI regularly to draft emails, quotes, or summaries, with some shared practices
Team-wide: AI is woven into real workflows across multiple roles, consistently producing output

text: How is AI being used to answer questions or pull information from your own documents, calls, or data?

options.label: It isn't: we look things up the old way or rely on memory
Some people use generic AI tools, but not with our actual business information
We summarize calls or look things up with AI occasionally, but it is not a standard practice
AI can answer from our own docs, call recordings, or CRM: it is part of how we work

text: When a proposal, email to a client, or internal report needs to be produced, what does that look like?

options.label: Written from scratch every time, by hand, by one person
Some templates exist, but it still takes significant manual effort
AI helps draft it, a person reviews and adjusts, time is meaningfully cut
AI produces a strong first draft from our context and templates; review takes minutes not hours

text: If a lead comes in at 10pm, what happens to it by the time your team starts work the next morning?

options.label: It sits until someone manually follows up, often the next day or later
An auto-reply goes out, but nothing else happens until a person picks it up
The lead is responded to automatically and added to a follow-up sequence, no human needed overnight
The lead is qualified, routed, and booked: a human only touches it if it needs a judgment call

text: Are there business events -- like a signed contract, a completed job, or a payment received -- that automatically trigger the next step without anyone having to remember to do it?

options.label: No: every next step requires a person to notice and act
Maybe one or two simple automations like a reminder email, but most handoffs are manual
Several automations run without human input, though some handoffs still require a person to close the loop
Yes: meaningful business processes run end-to-end without a human in the loop

text: How much repetitive, manually-executed work still consumes your team's hours each week?

options.label: Most of our time: nearly everything is done by hand
Significant: we have identified the bottlenecks but have not fixed them
Some: we automated the obvious things, a few stubborn manual steps remain
Minimal: we have systematically removed the repetitive work from our team's plates

text: Do you have any systems that can receive a goal, figure out the steps, and take multi-step actions across tools -- with human approval for the big calls?

options.label: No: all multi-step work requires a person to orchestrate each step
We use some AI tools in sequence, but a person is connecting the dots between each one
One or two workflows operate semi-autonomously: an agent does the steps, a human reviews before anything commits
Yes: goal-driven agents handle complex multi-step work with guardrails and human approval gates built in

text: Do you have visibility -- a dashboard or command center -- showing what your AI systems are doing, what they decided, and where they stopped for a human?

options.label: No: we have no real-time view into what automated systems are doing
We can check logs after the fact, but there is no live visibility
Some visibility exists for specific systems, but no unified view
Yes: we have a command-center view showing agent activity, decisions, and escalations in real time

text: When your automated systems hit an edge case they weren't built for, what happens?

options.label: They fail silently or do nothing: someone discovers it later
We get an error or notification, but there is no structured escalation
The system flags it and holds until a human decides, most of the time
Guardrails route it to a human with context: the agent hands off cleanly and resumes after approval

text: Do you know what AI tools your team is using, what they cost, and what data they can access?

options.label: No: employees use whatever they find, we have no inventory or oversight
Informal awareness: we know roughly what is being used but nothing is tracked or reviewed
We have a list of approved tools and a rough sense of spend, but it is not systematically reviewed
Yes: documented tool inventory, per-seat costs tracked, data access policies in place and reviewed regularly

text: Do you have guardrails around what AI can do with sensitive information -- customer data, financial records, confidential communications?

options.label: No guardrails: AI tools have access to whatever they can reach
We try to be careful but there is no written policy or enforced limit
Some guidelines exist, not consistently enforced or audited
Clear policy, enforced access controls, outputs audited regularly

text: Is there a specific person in your organization accountable for your AI roadmap and results?

options.label: No one: AI is everyone's side project and no one's responsibility
It comes up in leadership conversations, but no one formally owns it
Someone informally owns it, no defined outcomes or reporting
A named person or team owns AI adoption with defined outcomes they are measured on

text: Do you have a sequenced plan for where AI gets deployed next -- and is it tied to real business outcomes?

options.label: No plan: we act on whatever someone reads or suggests
General direction but no specific sequence or prioritization
A rough roadmap exists, but it has not been validated against ROI or re-sequenced recently
A prioritized roadmap tied to business outcomes, reviewed quarterly, with clear next steps
